text.tspan: The complement of “at least one of the lights is not green” is “none of the lights are not green.”
That has a double negative that we can clarify. If “none of the lights are not green,” then “all
the lights are green.” We calculated the probability of having all green lights in example 6.
So, there is about a 1% chance you will see all green lights, and about a 99% chance that you
will see at least one red light.
Why does this work? If we look at a probability distribution for the number of green lights (we will
create and use these in chapter 6), it will look like Table 10.
